tasks.short: Prepare price tickets and arrange merchandise into attractive, accessible displays.

steps.what: Read the display brief and promotion dates in {DOCS}.
Generate price tickets in the {OTHER} point-of-sale system.
Choose merchandise and adapt the display layout to available space.
Move merchandise, attach tickets and arrange the display.
Check ticket accuracy, visibility, stability and customer access before opening the display.

tasks.design: Configure {WORKFLOW} to turn promotion dates and approved briefs from {DOCS} into a dated display checklist. Configure the {OTHER} point-of-sale system to generate tickets from current prices; the sales assistant adapts the layout, installs the display and checks it before customers use it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Much of the task is physical. Briefs, promotion dates and ticket printing can also sit in separate places.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing templates, scheduling and price exports can handle preparation. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting them; it does not move merchandise.
tasks.still_hard: Space constraints, unstable items, missing stock and visual balance need attention on the shop floor.
tasks.human_edge: The sales assistant sees how customers move, notices awkward displays and makes practical aesthetic choices.

ambition.what: A weekly display adjustment based on aggregate product sell-through.

tasks.altitude: The week remains mostly physical display work, with less ticket preparation. The sales assistant can propose local layout changes; pricing and promotion authority do not change.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of retail sales workers
reach.task: Evaluate display performance and plan the next display change.
reach.learn: Read aggregate sell-through, distinguish stock shortages from weak presentation, and compare similar trading periods.

evidence.claim: Ticket templates and scheduled display checklists are feasible deterministic preparation aids; physical arrangement remains human.
The proposed time reductions and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.

assumptions: A central merchandising team supplies approved briefs and prices.
The {OTHER} point-of-sale system supports ticket templates or a usable price export.
Preparation occupies a small share of this task; the predominantly physical prior is retained.
The access estimate covers a shared checklist without individual performance tracking. National rules may require consultation if the scope changes.
Build ranges describe a small pilot, not a rollout across all stores.
unknowns: Which ticket formats and price-export interfaces are available?
Who may approve local display changes?
How often do promotion dates or printed prices conflict?
What access and consultation procedures apply?
research_questions: Can existing ticket configuration cover the required formats without custom code?
Which aggregate sales comparison would help staff assess display changes fairly?
new_work: Maintain ticket templates and promotion schedules.
Resolve missing prices and conflicting promotion dates.
Check that automated checklists reflect actual store space.

tasks.short: Count merchandise, resolve stock differences and request replenishment.

steps.what: Retrieve stock balances, sales and open deliveries from {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Count shelf and backroom merchandise using a handheld linked to {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Reconcile differences and confirm permitted stock corrections in {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Calculate replenishment quantities in {SPREADSHEET} using stock, demand and pack sizes.
Review quantities and approve the stock requisition in {PROCUREMENT}.
Submit approved orders through {PROCUREMENT} and record supplier acknowledgement.

tasks.design: Configure count lists, discrepancy queues and replenishment rules in {OPS_SYSTEM}, replacing the calculation in {SPREADSHEET}. A deterministic integration passes requisitions to {PROCUREMENT} and submits only approved orders, with duplicate checks and acknowledgement tracking. People count physical stock, resolve unexplained differences and approve spending.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock, incoming deliveries and purchasing approvals may be separated. Unreliable stock records make automatic replenishment difficult to trust.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing stock rules and purchasing workflows cover the calculations. AI-assisted coding can make the missing interfaces and validation cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Shrinkage, misplaced goods, seasonal demand and unreliable delivery dates can defeat otherwise correct calculations.
tasks.human_edge: Staff distinguish a counting error from damaged, misplaced or genuinely missing goods and anticipate local demand changes.

ambition.what: Daily review of likely stockouts before the next supplier delivery.

tasks.altitude: The sales assistant spends less time calculating and re-entering quantities and more time on stock exceptions. They gain scope to propose replenishment-rule changes; purchase approval remains with the authorised supervisor.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of retail sales workers
reach.task: Review stockout exposure and propose replenishment-rule changes.
reach.learn: Understand lead times, pack sizes, safety stock and the cash tied up in inventory.

reach.task: Resolve missing supplier acknowledgements and duplicate order risks.
reach.learn: Trace order identifiers, delivery commitments and cancellation status across records.

evidence.claim: Stock thresholds, pack-size calculations and approval routing can use deterministic rules without a model.
Physical counting and unexplained stock differences remain material human work.
The digest provides no documented implementation of this full retail replenishment design; estimates require pilot validation.

assumptions: Physical counts use a handheld linked to {OPS_SYSTEM}; {SPREADSHEET} bridges replenishment calculations to purchasing.
Existing replenishment configuration supports thresholds, lead times and pack sizes.
The sales assistant can confirm small stock corrections within delegated limits; larger differences are escalated.
Supplier submission supports stable order identifiers and acknowledgement checks.
The estimate covers one stock source and one purchasing connection.
Access includes stock and purchasing permissions. Consultation under national rules may apply if count records are used to monitor individuals.
unknowns: How accurate are stock balances and incoming delivery dates?
Which replenishment features are already licensed and configured?
What stock-correction and purchase-approval limits apply?
Which suppliers support electronic ordering and acknowledgements?
What employee consultation and access lead times apply?
research_questions: Can existing replenishment configuration remove the calculation workbook entirely?
What replay, duplicate and acknowledgement controls are supported by the available interfaces?
new_work: Investigate unmatched counts and stale delivery records.
Maintain replenishment thresholds, pack sizes and supplier lead times.
Handle failed submissions and missing acknowledgements.
Review whether proposed quantities create excess inventory.

tasks.short: Assess customer returns, approve remedies and process exchanges or refunds.

steps.what: Hear the customer's return request and clarify the desired remedy.
Find the purchase and payment in the {OTHER} point-of-sale system.
Inspect merchandise, accessories and the reported problem.
Apply return rules and agree an authorised remedy with the customer.
Resolve disputed or out-of-authority remedies with the customer.
Process the approved refund or exchange in the {OTHER} point-of-sale system.
Route returned merchandise to resale, quarantine or repair.

tasks.design: Configure the {OTHER} point-of-sale system to retrieve original purchases, calculate refund amounts and prepare linked stock movements and receipts. A versioned decision guide in {WORKFLOW} applies approved return rules from {DOCS}; the sales assistant inspects the goods, agrees the remedy and confirms payment execution. Exceptions go to the store supervisor with the purchase and inspection details already attached.
tasks.previous_blocker: Purchase lookup, return rules and exception approval may be disconnected. Item condition and customer expectations still require a conversation.
tasks.enabler_now: Linked transaction records and configurable return workflows can remove repeated entry. A deterministic guide can cover standard cases without interpreting unrestricted customer text.
tasks.still_hard: Missing purchase evidence, intermittent defects, disputed condition and consumer rights under national rules require careful handling.
tasks.human_edge: The sales assistant listens, assesses physical condition and explains a fair remedy when the customer's account and the records differ.

ambition.what: An arranged callback for unresolved product-fault returns.

tasks.altitude: The sales assistant spends less time retrieving transactions and entering refunds, leaving more time for difficult returns. Decision rights stay within existing remedy and payment limits; disputed cases remain with the supervisor.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of retail sales workers
reach.task: Review recurring return disputes and propose policy clarifications.
reach.learn: Separate statutory remedies from discretionary returns and use aggregate return reasons without profiling customers.

reach.task: Trace purchases made through another sales channel.
reach.learn: Match order, payment and fulfilment identifiers without creating duplicate refunds.

evidence.claim: A retailer support case combines fixed flows and FAQ retrieval, supporting structured guidance for routine questions.
That support case does not establish automated inspection, refund eligibility or payment execution for returns.
Linked purchase lookup, refund calculations and stock postings can be handled deterministically where interfaces permit.
GDPR Article 22 restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.

assumptions: The {OTHER} point-of-sale system holds original transaction and payment references.
Supervisor exception time is averaged across all returns; most returns skip that step.
Only the applicable approved remedy is required for processing.
Return rules reflect consumer rights under national rules and distinguish them from discretionary store policy.
The pilot uses transaction details needed for the return and preserves payment access controls.
Access estimates include refund permissions and review of any consultation required under national rules.
unknowns: Can purchases be retrieved across stores and sales channels?
Which remedies and refund amounts can each role authorise?
Which return configuration and payment interfaces are available?
How are fault inspections and disputed decisions recorded?
What retention, access and consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Can native return configuration cover the standard decision guide and prevent duplicate refunds?
What evidence must be retained for each remedy under the applicable national rules?
new_work: Maintain versioned return rules and approval limits.
Resolve unmatched purchases and failed refunds.
Check duplicate-refund controls and stock reversals.
Arrange and complete callbacks for unresolved faults.

tasks.short: Notice security risks, respond safely and record incidents.

steps.what: Observe the shop floor and notice possible theft or unsafe situations.
Assess immediate danger and decide whether to alert trained security staff.
De-escalate or handle the incident within training and legal authority.
Write factual observations and the outcome in an incident form in {DOCS}.
Review the incident and assign practical prevention or follow-up actions.

tasks.design: Configure a restricted incident form in {WORKFLOW}, with required factual fields, retention settings and follow-up reminders. Store approved procedures in {DOCS} and show aggregate incident categories in {BI}. Observation, risk assessment and intervention stay with trained people; the design adds no automated suspicion scoring or camera analysis.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recognising danger and responding safely depend on ambiguous physical events. Paperwork can be improved, but that does not solve observation or intervention.
tasks.enabler_now: Configurable forms and reminders can reduce reporting effort using existing technology. No model breakthrough is needed for this limited scope.
tasks.still_hard: False accusations, incomplete observations, confrontation and lawful evidence handling remain difficult. Staff must distinguish observed facts from assumptions.
tasks.human_edge: People judge immediate danger, respect dignity and adapt their response to a developing situation.

ambition.what: A weekly review of location-specific security hazards and prevention actions.

tasks.altitude: The week changes little beyond shorter incident paperwork and clearer follow-up. The sales assistant can contribute factual prevention proposals but gains no new authority to search, detain or exclude customers.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of retail sales workers
reach.task: Review incident patterns and assign store-layout or staffing remedies.
reach.learn: Use aggregate incident evidence, distinguish correlation from cause, and assess de-escalation options.

evidence.claim: The digest documents false alarms from behaviour-camera deployments, so detection alerts cannot be treated as established theft.
The digest documents an enforcement warning about facial recognition in a Dutch supermarket.
A multi-retailer study documents loss risks associated with self-checkout; automation does not remove security work.
Dutch works-council consent provisions cover certain employee-data and staff-monitoring arrangements; other countries have national rules.
Structured incident forms and reminders can reduce paperwork without automating judgements about people.

assumptions: Trained security support is available directly or through an escalation arrangement.
Observation time is an allocated share of concurrent shop-floor attention, not an additional continuous shift activity.
Incident-response and reporting shares are averaged across routine observation and actual incidents.
The proposed form records necessary factual observations with restricted access and retention under GDPR.
Consultation under national rules is assessed before rollout, especially if incident records could monitor employees.
The estimate covers forms and aggregate reporting; adding surveillance would require a separate assessment and estimate.
unknowns: What security support and escalation arrangements exist?
Which actions are staff trained and authorised to take?
What incident records, retention periods and access controls already exist?
Could the proposed reporting be used to monitor individual employees?
What consultation process and access approvals apply?
research_questions: Which form fields capture useful facts while avoiding unnecessary personal data?
Which aggregate incident categories support practical prevention without identifying staff or customers?
new_work: Maintain incident categories, access permissions and retention settings.
Correct reports that mix observations with unsupported allegations.
Follow up prevention actions and overdue reviews.
Refresh escalation contacts and practical staff training.

role.altitude: The role remains centred on customers and physical merchandise. Less preparation and transaction entry create room for stock exceptions, difficult returns and small display improvements; financial and security authority remain within existing limits.
reach: Support the retail supervisor's stockout and display reviews using aggregate sales and stock evidence.
Help order clerks resolve purchase traces, supplier acknowledgements and return transaction mismatches.
Contribute factual incident patterns to the retail supervisor's prevention planning.
skills_to_grow: Stock reconciliation, lead times and replenishment economics.
Consumer remedies under national rules and clear explanations of return decisions.
Aggregate sales analysis and practical display evaluation.
De-escalation, factual incident reporting and careful handling of personal data.
role.ambitious_version: A sales assistant who combines customer service with a regular improvement brief: identify a stockout risk, test a display change, resolve a recurring return problem and propose a practical safety improvement.
